instructions:
Turn on treesitter beyond the defaults, and fold by syntax.

1. Explore first: open ~/.config/nvim/init.lua (Lua already has treesitter on) and run
   :InspectTree. Move around in the tree and watch the cursor in the source follow.
   Close it with q. Put the cursor inside a function argument, press v, then an an an:
   the selection grows node by node. in shrinks it back.
2. Enable treesitter highlighting for the other parsers that ship with Neovim (C and Vimscript):
     vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('FileType', {
       group = grp,                     -- your augroup from 10.3
       pattern = { 'c', 'vim' },
       callback = function() vim.treesitter.start() end,
     })
3. Syntax-aware folding (folds start open):
     vim.opt.foldmethod = 'expr'
     vim.opt.foldexpr = 'v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr()'
     vim.opt.foldlevel = 99
   Try it in init.lua: zc closes the block you're in, zo opens it, za toggles, zM/zR close/open all.
4. Optional, for more languages (TypeScript, Python, ...): the nvim-treesitter plugin installs more parsers.
   Its current version needs the `tree-sitter` CLI and a C compiler (e.g. gcc).
   See https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter. Not needed to pass this lesson.

Read more: :help treesitter-highlight, :help vim.treesitter.foldexpr(), :help v_an, :help fold-commands

# --- shared helpers (read-only checks) ---
fail=0
ok()  { printf '  \033[32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() { printf '  \033[31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; [ -n "$2" ] && printf '      → %s\n' "$2"; fail=1; }
# q 'lua expression' : evaluate with your real config, print the result
q() { nvim --headless -c "lua io.stdout:write(tostring($1))" -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null; }
CFG=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("config"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
DATA=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("data"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
startup_errors() { nvim --headless -c 'qa!' 2>&1 | grep -iE 'error|E[0-9]{3,4}:' | head -5; }
finish() { if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "All checks passed."; exit 0; else echo "Not done yet - fix the ✘ items and run: vimdrill --check"; exit 1; fi; }
# ---

fq() { # fq <file> <lua-expr> [wait-ms]
  nvim --headless "$1" -c "lua vim.wait(${3:-300}, function() return false end); io.stdout:write(tostring($2))" -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null
}

echo "Checking treesitter setup"
t=$(mktemp -d); printf 'int main(void) {\n  return 0;\n}\n' > "$t/a.c"; printf 'let x = 1\n' > "$t/a.vim"
[ "$(fq "$t/a.c" 'vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()] ~= nil')" = true ] \
  && ok "treesitter highlighting active in C files" || bad "no treesitter highlighting in a .c file" "FileType autocmd with vim.treesitter.start() (step 2)"
[ "$(fq "$t/a.vim" 'vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()] ~= nil')" = true ] \
  && ok "treesitter highlighting active in Vimscript files" || bad "no treesitter highlighting in a .vim file" "add 'vim' to the pattern"
[ "$(fq "$t/a.c" 'vim.wo.foldmethod')" = expr ] && ok "foldmethod=expr" || bad "foldmethod isn't expr" "vim.opt.foldmethod = 'expr'"
fq "$t/a.c" 'vim.wo.foldexpr' | grep -q 'treesitter' && ok "treesitter foldexpr" || bad "foldexpr isn't treesitter's" "vim.opt.foldexpr = 'v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr()'"
l=$(fq "$t/a.c" 'vim.wo.foldlevel'); [ "${l:-0}" -ge 20 ] && ok "folds start open (foldlevel=$l)" || bad "foldlevel=${l:-0}: files open fully folded" "vim.opt.foldlevel = 99"
rm -rf "$t"
finish

instructions:
Hook up a real language server. This lesson uses TypeScript as the example.
Since TypeScript 7 (the native port), the compiler itself is the language server: tsc --lsp --stdio.

1. Install it (needs Node.js with npm):
     npm install -g typescript
   Check: tsc --version   (should print 7.x)
2. Create ~/.config/nvim/lsp/tsc.lua:
     return {
       cmd = { 'tsc', '--lsp', '--stdio' },
       filetypes = { 'javascript', 'javascriptreact', 'typescript', 'typescriptreact' },
       root_markers = { 'tsconfig.json', 'package.json', '.git' },
     }
3. In init.lua:
     vim.lsp.enable('tsc')
4. Open any .ts file in a project and run :checkhealth vim.lsp. Under "Active Clients"
   you should see tsc. Try K on a symbol.
   (Using the nvim-lspconfig plugin instead of writing step 2 is fine too: it provides
   lsp/tsc.lua, and you still need vim.lsp.enable('tsc').)
5. Projects pinned to TypeScript 5.x need the older typescript-language-server + ts_ls
   setup instead. Any server that attaches to .ts files passes this check.

Read more: :help lsp-quickstart, :help lsp-config, :help vim.lsp.enable()

# --- shared helpers (read-only checks) ---
fail=0
ok()  { printf '  \033[32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
bad() { printf '  \033[31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; [ -n "$2" ] && printf '      → %s\n' "$2"; fail=1; }
# q 'lua expression' : evaluate with your real config, print the result
q() { nvim --headless -c "lua io.stdout:write(tostring($1))" -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null; }
CFG=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("config"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
DATA=$(nvim --headless --clean -c 'lua io.stdout:write(vim.fn.stdpath("data"))' -c 'qa!' 2>/dev/null)
startup_errors() { nvim --headless -c 'qa!' 2>&1 | grep -iE 'error|E[0-9]{3,4}:' | head -5; }
finish() { if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "All checks passed."; exit 0; else echo "Not done yet - fix the ✘ items and run: vimdrill --check"; exit 1; fi; }
# ---

echo "Checking LSP"
if command -v tsc >/dev/null; then
  v=$(tsc --version 2>/dev/null | grep -o '[0-9][0-9.]*' | head -1)
  [ "${v%%.*}" -ge 7 ] 2>/dev/null && ok "tsc $v (has --lsp)" \
    || printf '  - tsc %s has no --lsp: fine if typescript-language-server attaches instead (step 5)\n' "$v"
else
  printf '  - tsc not found: fine if another TypeScript server attaches (step 5)\n'
fi
t=$(mktemp -d); echo '{}' > "$t/package.json"; printf 'const n: number = 1;\nexport { n };\n' > "$t/a.ts"
out=$(cd "$t" && nvim --headless a.ts -c 'lua vim.wait(20000, function() return #vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = 0 }) > 0 end, 200); local c = vim.lsp.get_clients({ bufnr = 0 }); io.stdout:write("CLIENT=" .. (#c > 0 and c[1].name or "none"))' -c 'qa!' 2>&1)
rm -rf "$t"
c=$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -o 'CLIENT=[^ ]*' | cut -d= -f2)
err=$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -o 'message = "[^"]*' | head -1 | cut -c12-)
[ -n "$c" ] && [ "$c" != none ] && ok "a language server ($c) attaches to .ts files" \
  || bad "no LSP client attached to a .ts file within 20s${err:+ - server said: $err}" "steps 2-3, then :checkhealth vim.lsp in a .ts file"
finish

instructions:
Practice the LSP keys on a small TypeScript project.

0. Run `vimdrill --check` once. It creates the project in ~/vim-mastery/practice/11.3
   (and reports "not done yet"). To start over: rm -rf that folder and run --check again.
1. cd ~/vim-mastery/practice/11.3 && nvim src/main.ts
2. Diagnostics: ]d jumps to the first error, Ctrl-w d shows the full message.
   There are two problems: formatPrice isn't imported, and `total` has the wrong type.
3. On formatPrice, press gra and pick the import fix (it reads 'Update import from "./cart"',
   because main.ts already imports from there).
4. Fix `const total: string` to `number` (ciw...). ]d should now find nothing.
5. Ctrl-] on `calc` jumps to its definition in cart.ts. Press grn THERE and rename it to
   calculateTotal. The import and the call in main.ts change too. Ctrl-o takes you back.
   (Renaming at the call site in main.ts only adds a local alias, `calc as calculateTotal`.)
6. Explore without a check: K on Item (hover), grr on Item (references, then :cnext/:cclose),
   gO (outline), Ctrl-s inside calculateTotal( ... ) in insert mode.
7. :wa to save everything, then vimdrill --check.

Read more: :help lsp-defaults, :help diagnostic-defaults

Completion as you type, plus surround. Commenting (gc) is already built in.

1. Built-in LSP completion. In init.lua:
     vim.opt.completeopt = { 'menuone', 'noselect', 'popup' }
     vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('LspAttach', {
       group = grp,
       callback = function(ev)
         local client = vim.lsp.get_client_by_id(ev.data.client_id)
         if client and client:supports_method('textDocument/completion') then
           vim.lsp.completion.enable(true, client.id, ev.buf, { autotrigger = true })
         end
       end,
     })
   In a .ts file, type `items.` and the menu appears. Ctrl-n/Ctrl-p to move, Ctrl-y to accept,
   Ctrl-e to cancel. (blink.cmp is a popular plugin alternative. If you use it, this check
   accepts that instead.)
2. Surround: add to your lazy spec
     { 'kylechui/nvim-surround', event = 'VeryLazy', opts = {} },
   (mini.surround is accepted too, but its keys are sa/sd/sr, not ys/ds/cs.)
3. Try them in any file:
     ysiw"   quote a word           cs"'   double to single quotes
     ds"     remove the quotes      yss)   wrap the whole line in ( )
     gcc     toggle a line comment  gcip   comment a paragraph   gcgc  uncomment a block

Read more: :help lsp-completion, :help ins-completion, :help commenting, :help nvim-surround

1. Comment out the two print lines (gcc).
2. Uncomment the old function block in one go (gcgc).
3. Rename M.old to M.legacy.

start.main.lua:

function M.setup()
  print("debug 1")
  vim.opt.number = true
  print("debug 2")
end
